content.content:
Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node, reading it against squvoxyr, then sqwusxql; nothing runs, and no behaviour is probed.

(1) Subject. A decision whose content is still a placeholder or otherwise records no commitment leaves the check with no subject to read; that absence is a finding, named as such.

(2) The entry whose presentation the name serves (squvoxyr). That decision commits the entry at issue to reading as a visible link, keeps the entry's text as the bare id it is, and expressly leaves the entry's colour, cursor, hover, focus, carrying element and class vocabulary to the decisions that own them. Fail on any element of the dependent that re-decides one of those for the entry: one that requires, forbids or spells out the entry's look, one that changes or replaces the entry's text, one that adds an activation, an input, a label, an icon or a second surface beside it, one that fixes a declaration for it (a colour or colour role, a cursor, a hover state, a focus marker, a decoration, a weight or a spacing), and one that attaches the name to something other than that entry — the paths, the block, the section's frame or its other text. If that decision carries no recorded commitment about such an entry, the use has nothing to be read against, and that absence is a finding.

(3) The name the dependent fixes (sqwusxql). That decision fixes two class names with the case each denotes, keeps their use exhaustive and exclusive over the entries it governs, forbids multiplying them into further classes, modifiers, data attributes, element ids or other hooks, and requires a finer distinction to be settled as its own decision instead of being spelled out of those two. Fail on any element of the dependent that spells its name out of either recorded name — a modifier or qualifier appended to one, one name nested inside the other's block, or a derivation that reads as one of them plus an addition; one that puts either recorded name on the entry at issue, beside the dependent's name or in its place; one that states a further modifier, a data attribute, an element id or an additional hook for the distinction it draws; or one that defers the distinction to a decision the graph does not hold rather than settling it here.

(4) The mapping the vocabulary carries (sqwusxql). Fail on any element of the dependent that changes, extends, narrows or restates which case either recorded name denotes or which entries carry either name, or that reads that pair as the case its own entry falls into.

(5) One name across both carriers. Where the dependent states what the entry carries and what the stylesheet's rules select, fail on any element that names one class for the entry and selects a different name, or a different form of that name, in the rules, or that lets the rules reach the entry through anything other than the class the entry carries — an element, a structural position, a state or a second class — since a name its own selection does not read cannot be what decides which of the rules reach the entry.

(6) Non-contradiction. No element of the dependent contradicts squvoxyr or sqwusxql. Fail on any contradicting element, naming it and the prerequisite involved.

(7) Decidability. From the recorded statement alone a reviewer must be able to name an observation that would refute it without supplying a rule the dependent does not state — an observation about the name the entry carries, or about which of the stylesheet's rules reach it. If no such observation can be named from the statement, that is a finding.
content.rationale:
Both prerequisites are inline prose commitments — squvoxyr states that a ref-path entry reads as a visible link rather than as bare text and leaves the entry's vocabulary to another decision, sqwusxql states the two names a listed entry carries and that a carrier needing a finer distinction settles it as its own decision — and the dependent is inline prose naming the class such an entry carries and the one name the stylesheet's rules select, so this edge is the evaluation matrix's natural-to-natural cell and takes the gate form: a reviewer reads the recorded decision against the recorded prerequisites and checks non-violation, and nothing runs. A runnable check would have to probe the markup and the stylesheet for a prose child, which the strictness rule denies, and it would have to fix as an observable a name the dependent is otherwise free to state; the layer of the child, not the convenience of a test, is what selects this form.

Bare license would leave the two ways this decision can actually go wrong ungated. The first is the naming: the vocabulary's two names denote two cases and are exhaustive over the entries they govern, so a decision that re-used one of them for this entry, or arrived at its name by appending a modifier, by nesting, or by deriving one of them plus an addition, would put the entry into a case the vocabulary never defined and make a name mean two things at once — the very crossing sqwusxql exists to prevent. The second is drift between the carriers: a decision that names one class for the entry while the rules select another name, or reach the entry through an element, a structure or a state instead, has named a class that selects nothing, so the entry's look would be decided by whatever rules happen to fall on it. Clause (3) and clause (5) check exactly those two, from the vocabulary's own statements rather than from any rule of this check.

Against squvoxyr the criteria hold the line at the presentation it owns and leaves: the entry, its bare-id text and its look stay that decision's, and the dependent's commitment is the name by which the appearance decisions reach that entry, not a second decision about how it looks or what it shows. Fixing a colour, a cursor, a hover or focus mark, or a decoration here would contradict the division those decisions record, and attaching the name to the paths, the block or the section frame would mark something other than the entry that decision presents. Clause (7) keeps the whole thing decidable at review time: a statement of naming from which no refuting observation can be named has settled nothing a reviewer can check.

Every clause is decidable by reading two or three recorded nodes, names no endpoint-specific element in advance — which name or element fails is the check's output, never the criterion — demands no wording of the dependent, and states no rule its prerequisites do not, so it survives the dependent being rewritten without changing what it decides.
